description: Run SQL across in-memory dataframes. Dataframes auto-populate when find_* tools spill (named `df_<uuid>`) — the dataframe name appears inline on every find_* response that spilled (`result.dataframe.tableName`), so the typical flow is find_* → read the name → query here. Use brapi_dataframe_describe to inspect schema and provenance for a known name. SELECT only — writes/DDL/COPY/PRAGMA/ATTACH/file-reads are rejected. Use SQL as the paging idiom: `LIMIT/OFFSET` to walk results, projection to trim columns, aggregation to summarize. Use `registerAs` to chain — the result lands as a new dataframe.

preview.description: Cap the number of rows returned in this response. A value above `rowLimit` (or, when `rowLimit` is omitted, above the deployment-wide response cap) returns rows up to that ceiling. When omitted, the ceiling applies. Lower this with `registerAs` when you only need a sample to verify the query.

registerAs.description: Persist the full result as a new dataframe under this name. The response is bounded by preview and a 24,000-byte row budget. Conflicts fail — choose a different name, or remove the existing dataframe with brapi_dataframe_drop where this deployment enables it. Identifier rules: letters, digits, and underscores; must start with a letter or underscore; max 63 characters.

rowLimit.description: Hard cap on rows materialized into the response, bounded by the deployment-wide response cap. For larger result sets, use `registerAs` to keep the full result queryable instead of raising this.

sql.description: SELECT statement against dataframes. Single statement only — writes, DDL, DESCRIBE / SUMMARIZE, file reads, and exports are rejected. Use brapi_dataframe_describe to discover available dataframes. SQL is the primary paging idiom: use `LIMIT/OFFSET` to walk a large dataframe, projection to trim columns, and aggregation (`COUNT`, `GROUP BY`, `AVG`) to summarize without materializing every row.

name: brapi_dataframe_query

cap.description: Row ceiling that bound the response: the smallest of preview, rowLimit, and the deployment-wide response cap.

columns.description: Column names and types in projection order, enough to write a follow-up query.

items.description: One column descriptor — name and SQL/DuckDB type.

type.description: DuckDB column type (e.g. VARCHAR, BIGINT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, JSON), the same with or without `registerAs`.

dataframe.description: Name of the dataframe holding the full result, populated when `registerAs` was supplied. Reference this name in follow-up queries.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `sql_rejected`: SQL broke the read-only rules: more than one statement, a non-SELECT, a disallowed operation or function, a file or URL named as a table, a system-catalog read, or a DESCRIBE, SUMMARIZE, or SHOW statement. `sql_execution_error`: The SELECT passed the read-only rules but failed while running on the staged data, such as a cast of a value that does not convert. `missing_table`: The SQL names a dataframe this workspace does not hold, because it expired, was dropped, or the name is mistyped. `register_as_clash`: The registerAs name is already taken by a dataframe in this workspace. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance for reaching the rows this response left out.

rowCount.description: Total rows the query produced (may exceed `rows.length` when capped).

rows.description: Leading rows bounded by preview/rowLimit and 24,000 bytes on each serialized row representation. May be empty when the first row is oversized.

items.description: One result row. Columns are projected from the SQL SELECT clause; call brapi_dataframe_describe to inspect source dataframe schemas.

truncated.description: True when the response carries fewer rows than the query produced.

title: Brapi Dataframe Query
